h1:
Tha Chin River Fish
8 Riverside Spots Worth Trying
intro: The Tha Chin River runs straight through the middle of Suphan Buri, north to south, and that's exactly why the food this province is best known for is freshwater fish. Snakehead, soldier fish, redtail catfish, butter catfish and clown knifefish get pulled out and turned into fragrant grilled fish, sharp tom yum and rich choo chee curry. We've picked the places people in Suphan Buri actually eat at — both right on the Tha Chin River and out among the rice paddies beyond town — and noted what each one does best.

blocks.html: Ask anyone from Suphan Buri what to feed visiting friends and the answer almost always circles back to river fish. The town sits on the Tha Chin River as its main artery, with fish ponds ringing the outskirts, so the fish is fresh and cheaper than you'd pay in Bangkok. The dishes you'll find at nearly every spot are grilled snakehead (usually wrapped in straw and grilled, or packed in salt), tom yum with soldier fish or redtail catfish, and butter catfish choo chee. Here are the 8 places we'd point you to, with what each one is known for.

blocks.text: What Tha Chin River Fish You'll Find

blocks.html: Before you sit down, it helps to know the popular fish — ordering gets a whole lot easier.

items: Snakehead — the province's star fish. Firm, sweet flesh, usually grilled whole and eaten with seafood dipping sauce and boiled vegetables, or done as steamed snakehead with lime and garlic.
Soldier fish — soft flesh, few bones, at its best in tom yum. Most people coming to Suphan Buri order soldier-fish tom yum as their main dish.
Redtail catfish — a big skin-fish with just the right richness, good for tom yum, pad cha and frying alike.
Butter catfish — thin, soft flesh that melts in your mouth, makes the best choo chee.
Clown knifefish — chewy, springy flesh, scraped and turned into fish cakes or knifefish meatballs blanched for dipping.
River prawns — a bonus from the Tha Chin, grilled whole with the head fat oozing, or fried with garlic.

blocks.text: 8 River-Fish Spots Locals in Suphan Buri Actually Eat At

items.name: Rabiang Nam – Kung Pen (on the Tha Chin River)
items.blurb: A comfortable spot right on the Tha Chin River with a deck jutting out over the water. It's strong on both rich grilled river prawns and a long list of river-fish dishes — thick, aromatic soldier-fish tom yum, sharp snakehead larb-style salad, and redtail catfish pad cha with real heat. Great for coming with a big table.
items.meta: Phai Khwang, Mueang district · Open 10.00–21.00 · Tel 035-504-273

items.name: Khrua Kang Na (Song Phi Nong)
items.blurb: A Thai wooden-house place set among green rice paddies, easy to spot from the road. You sit in open-sided sala pavilions catching the breeze off the fields. It's known for big straw-grilled paddy snakehead, straw-baked chicken, redtail catfish tom yum and climbing-perch choo chee. A nice spot for photos and settling in with family for a long lunch.
items.meta: Song Phi Nong district · rice-paddy restaurant
items.price: Big grilled fish ~฿280 · straw-baked chicken ~฿150

items.name: Phai Khwang
items.blurb: A legendary old-timer in Suphan Buri that families keep coming back to, visit after visit. There's an open-air section and an air-conditioned room. It's strong on salt-fried prawns, grilled snakehead eaten with chilli dip and boiled veg, and redtail catfish tom yum — the cooking has stayed consistent for years.
items.meta: Suphan Buri–Pa Mok Rd, ~2 km past the town junction · Tel 035-523-014

items.name: Ruean Phae Khrua Suphan (on the Tha Chin)
items.blurb: A floating-raft restaurant on the Tha Chin River where you eat out on the raft in the cool breeze. The big orders here are sharp soldier-fish tom yum and horseshoe-crab papaya salad with its distinctive aroma. A good pick for a relaxed evening watching the light play on the water.
items.meta: On the Tha Chin River · seating on a floating raft

items.name: Kung Pen Sam Chuk (Jay Noei)
items.blurb: On the bank of the Tha Chin River near Sam Chuk, an easy walk on from the 100-year-old market. It's known for butter catfish choo chee so soft it melts, clown knifefish cakes, snail kua curry, and river prawns done several ways — grilled, fried with garlic, or fried in fish sauce.
items.meta: Sam Chuk district, on the Tha Chin River · near Sam Chuk Market

items.name: Khanap Nam Suphan Buri
items.blurb: A pleasant spot right by the water, strong on fragrant grilled snakehead cooked just to that sweet, perfectly-done point, plus springy prawns marinated raw in fish sauce. When you're full there's a cute little café corner to settle into for coffee — good for a group that wants to eat and then linger.
items.meta: In Suphan Buri town · has a café corner

items.name: Phae Ahan Phan Mai Sai Nam
items.blurb: A floating food-raft on the Tha Chin River. The draw is genuinely fresh river fish because you're right on the water — done grilled, in tom yum, or stir-fried plenty of ways. You sit on the raft over a wide stretch of river, good for coming as a group or booking a table for a special occasion.
items.meta: On the Tha Chin River · seating on a raft

items.name: Mae Buai
items.blurb: The place people in Suphan Buri think of when it comes to fish. It's known for bouncy, made-fresh clown knifefish meatballs and a soldier-fish tom yum with fresh fish and a well-rounded, sharp broth. A reliable spot for anyone who wants good freshwater fish without rolling the dice.

blocks.title: How to Order Without Overpaying
blocks.html: Most fish places price grilled fish by the size of the fish (weighed by the kilo). If there are only a few of you, ask the staff to pick a medium fish — it'll be just right and won't blow the budget. Order one grilled fish, one pot of tom yum and one plate of choo chee, then add a stir-fried vegetable and an omelette and the whole table is full.

blocks.text: How to Pick a Spot for Your Trip

items.name: Want a river view
items.blurb: Rabiang Nam–Kung Pen, Ruean Phae Khrua Suphan, or Phae Ahan Phan Mai Sai Nam — all right on the Tha Chin, catching the cool breeze in the evening.

items.name: Want a rice-paddy feel
items.blurb: Khrua Kang Na in Song Phi Nong, a Thai wooden house out among the fields — good for photos and letting the kids run around.

items.name: Doing Sam Chuk and need a meal
items.blurb: Kung Pen Sam Chuk sits by the water near the 100-year-old market — finish wandering the market and stop in for fish right after.

blocks.html: Riverside spots are at their best in the late afternoon once the sun softens and the breeze off the river turns cool. Weekends, Saturday and Sunday, get busy, especially the well-known ones like Phai Khwang and Khrua Kang Na. If you're going as a group or for a weekend lunch, booking a table ahead is the easier call. A big grilled fish takes a while to cook, so order it first and put in your other dishes after — that way you're not hungry for long.

faq.q: Which Tha Chin River fish dishes should I order?
faq.a: The dishes people in Suphan Buri order most are grilled snakehead (usually wrapped in straw and grilled, or packed in salt), tom yum with soldier fish or redtail catfish, and butter catfish choo chee. If you like fried food, add clown knifefish cakes and grilled river prawns.

faq.q: Where are the nicest riverside fish spots on the Tha Chin?
faq.a: There are several along the Tha Chin River — Rabiang Nam–Kung Pen at Phai Khwang, Ruean Phae Khrua Suphan, and Kung Pen Sam Chuk near the 100-year-old Sam Chuk market. Pick whichever fits the route you've planned.

faq.q: Roughly how much does eating Suphan Buri river fish cost?
faq.a: Most of the time it works out to around ฿200–500 per person, depending on how big a grilled fish you order — grilled fish is priced by weight. If there are only a few of you, pick a medium fish and order one pot of tom yum and you'll eat well without blowing the budget.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table ahead?
faq.a: On weekdays you usually don't need to book, but on Saturdays, Sundays and weekend lunches the popular spots get busy. If you're going as a big group or want a riverside table, booking ahead is the safer bet.

faq.q: Coming to Suphan Buri for a day — where can I sightsee and then stop for fish?
faq.a: Do the 100-year-old Sam Chuk market in the daytime, then stop for fish by the water around Sam Chuk right after. Or if you're sightseeing in town, finish with an evening meal at a Tha Chin riverside spot once the sun softens and the breeze cools.
